A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAGREF, with matching masked-guidance components and single-ID/multi-subject evaluations. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–F were included in the comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results in Table 1, generated examples and qualitative component ablations in Figure 9.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–4, a human preference study, and additional qualitative analyses and failure cases.

M1.justification: V2 retains masked channel concatenation but adds subject disentanglement: text-derived cross-attention value embeddings are injected into corresponding subject regions at each layer. It also extends the three-stage data pipeline with generative cross-pair augmentation of face, object and background references. These change the procedure beyond expanded documentation.

E1.justification: The benchmark retains 60 single-ID and 60 multi-subject cases. V2 adds background references to augmented training, whereas v1 explicitly describes training without background conditioning. Figures 9–11 extend qualitative coverage to clothing, eyewear and accessory transfer, including cluttered reference images, within the existing any-reference generation task.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparisons retain the same twelve single-ID and six multi-subject baselines. However, v2 Figure 6 reduces the single-ID qualitative comparison from v1 Figure 7, omitting HunyuanCustom, Concat-ID, EchoVideo, FantasyID, VACE and Vidu 2.0. These methods remain in the numerical evaluation.

E3.justification: V2 replaces optical-flow motion magnitude with Motion Smoothness, adds Subj-Sim and Bg-Sim, and introduces an averaged Total Score. New experiments include an ablation with matched training steps/resources and a 30-participant pairwise study with 60 questions per questionnaire and a tie option. Cross-pair augmentation also changes training preprocessing.

E4.justification: V1's qualitative masking/concatenation ablation is retained as v2 Figure 7. V2 additionally provides quantitative training-paradigm and pipeline ablations in Tables 3–4, semantic-alignment heatmaps and subject-disentanglement comparisons in Figures 4 and 8, and explicit failure cases in Figure 14. These substantially expand component validation and error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2's participant counts and preference percentages describe the new study but do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1 reports MAGREF FaceSim scores of 0.567/0.581 for single-ID/multi-subject generation; v2's revised evaluation reports ID-Sim scores of 0.595/0.542. Numerous baseline entries change, and the reported single-ID identity leader changes from VACE to MAGREF. V2 adds subject/background scores, quantitative ablations, preference outcomes and qualitative findings. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 introduces the subject-specific mask and masked semantic-value update in Equations 5–6, a limited substantive mathematical extension. Most other added equations formalize previously described operations or standard background. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion redefine the contribution around masked guidance, semantic subject disentanglement and cross-pair data construction, explicitly targeting subject confusion and copy-paste artifacts. V1 centers its contributions on masking and channel concatenation. Its explicit claim of generalization from single-subject training is dropped.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking semantic injection to reduced subject interference and augmented reference pairs to reduced copying. Appendices E.2 and F expand v1's broad backbone-quality caveat into specific limitations involving complex interactions, physical behavior, reference-count scaling, T5 understanding and controllable long-video generation.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add extensive processing and evaluation documentation, including baseline checkpoints, output resolutions/frame rates and identity-metric frame sampling. Conversely, v1's 22-million-to-0.5-million training-data counts, 32-H100/four-day budget and 480P/81-frame training settings disappear. V2 specifies H100 80GB GPUs and PyTorch but leaves its augmentation model and injection strength unspecified.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage remains broadly similar. V2 adds citations including CINEMA, OpenS2V-Nexus, Flow Matching, SDXL, SAM2 and Q-Align, while removing OpenCV and Open-Sora. These are localized updates supporting the revised method and evaluation.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract and introduction around three challenges, extends the title, moves data curation after the generation mechanisms, combines qualitative and quantitative discussion into Main Results, and organizes detailed material into six appendices. This substantially changes the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column paper to a single-column report. V2 redraws and combines method diagrams, expands the pipeline illustration, splits the main results table, adds ablation tables, preference/radar plots, heatmaps and failure panels, and relocates retained qualitative material into new figure arrangements.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–4 address v1's lack of quantitative component validation, while subject/background metrics, human preference evidence and explicit failure analysis substantially strengthen evaluation of any-reference generation. These gains outweigh the loss of training-data counts and compute details. Reproducibility remains weakened by the unspecified augmentation model and injection strength, and neither version quantifies uncertainty, but v2 provides substantially stronger support and clearer boundaries for its contributions.
